shortfalls.title: Keyboard cancellation can stop the wrong task.
A capitalized field in a record request can write the wrong field.
Saving a reused name silently overwrites a saved entry.
A temporary storage failure leaves abandoned work looking active.
Valid bot names can push chat controls outside a narrow window.
A cancellation click can disappear while a chat action is in flight.
The open page continues to report live progress when the server is down.
Reloading loses the reading position and unsent text.
Common opening questions make saved conversations indistinguishable.
An incomplete clarification loses the pending record request.
Active instructions cannot be cleared from an existing bot.
Approval previews can make field boundaries ambiguous.
A total above the safe integer range can be silently rounded on update.
The composer silently drops the tail of overlong input.
Setup gives no reason when the environment token is rejected.

choices.text: The initial conversation title comes from the first sent message
A new bot starts with one empty conversation.
Saved instructions and saved tasks are per-person libraries
Bot names and saved-entry names are limited to 80 characters.
Conversationally remembered facts are deduplicated case-insensitively
An approval compares the proposed field's original value with its current value.
Existing record identity, type and reader fields are immutable through the chat.
Both a saved setup token and an accepted environment token configure the whole installation.
Several long tasks can run in one conversation.
The return summary uses the browser's last-seen time for each person
Dark mode is a browser preference shared by profiles using that browser.
Draft text follows its conversation when switching threads in the same open tab.
